brand.identity: Red Horizon is a clearly fictional, AI-assisted Mars exploration project. Its mark is a rust-red Mars planet with a highlighted chain of low Martian hills within it, seen at sunrise against a sparse black sky with a legible distant Earth and smaller Moon. The circle must unmistakably read as Mars, never the rising Sun itself. It is an emblem, not a real agency seal, flag, or government mark.
brand.instruction: Create one square, text-free logo mark on a clean black background. Centre one large rust-red Mars circle. Across the upper-middle of that circle, draw a restrained segmented Martian relief band: four to six low connected hill forms, following the circle's general curvature. Slightly left of centre place one broad, low shield-volcano rise inspired by Olympus Mons—wide and gently sloping, never a sharp cone—with two or three smaller eroded ridges on either side. The lower region is deep oxide red and the upper region is a lighter dusty-red Mars tone; use one narrow lighter rim highlight only to make the relief clear. The relief remains entirely inside the complete circle and must feel like the planet's horizon, not a landscape illustration. Place a compact warm pale-yellow Sun partly hidden behind the upper-left rim of Mars: its lower half is occluded by the planet. Add a restrained golden-orange halo around the exposed Sun and a subtle amber bloom along the nearby Mars rim and first relief ridge; no rays, lens flare, or dramatic glow. High to the right place one clear pale-blue Earth dot at logo-readable symbolic scale; place a smaller dim blue-gray Moon point a short distance below-right of Earth. Flat vector-like geometry, exact spacing, crisp edges, solid fills with only the controlled sunrise glow, no texture, no shadows, no stars beyond the Earth/Moon pair, no spacecraft, no rover, no astronaut, no flags, no official seals, no letters, no words, no numbers, no watermark.
brand.style: Minimal, clear, vector-friendly space-mission identity: deep oxide red and dusty red inside a Mars circle, a restrained pale rim highlight over its segmented relief, sunrise amber at the upper-left edge, a legible pale-blue Earth point and dim blue-gray Moon point, and black negative space. Contemporary technical editorial design, generous breathing room, high contrast, exact simple shapes, no pseudo-text or decorative illustration. The internal Martian relief and sunrise are the defining Red Horizon details.
variants: Use a perfectly balanced centred Mars circle. Place a broad Olympus Mons-like shield rise slightly left of centre, then let the terrain descend into three smaller irregular low ridges across the circle. Let the Sun emerge behind the upper-left rim with a controlled warm halo, and retain a clear Earth with its dimmer Moon high in the upper-right.

rh01.identity: RH-01 Pathfinder: a compact fictional robotic Mars survey rover. Low roughly two-metre-class warm-white equipment body with muted red identification panels and a dark instrument deck. Six broad metal-mesh wheels on visible articulated suspension. One short central mast with a compact stereo-camera pair. One front-centre two-joint arm ending in a small contact tool, folded into a travel cradle when not working. Matte ceramic coating, brushed metal arm, protected dark pivots, restrained seams and fasteners. No cockpit, passengers, cabin, windows, weapons, tracks, legs, hover hardware, decorative fins, extra arms, loose cables, or fantasy energy parts.
rh01.canonical_instruction: Front-left three-quarter reference view at body height. Entire rover visible on a seamless neutral white floor and white background, with a faint grounded contact shadow. Fold the single front-centre arm into its travel cradle. Keep all six mesh wheels, visible articulated suspension, mast, and dark instrument deck mechanically coherent and readable. This is a fictional engineering reference candidate, not an official agency image.
rh01.scene_instruction: A calm first field-check scene on a broad rusty Martian plain. RH-01 is stationary, seen from front-left with the whole rover visible. Fine ochre dust lightly touches the lower panels and mesh-wheel contact patches; the mast is upright and the arm stays folded. Dark basalt fragments, subtle shallow tracks, and a low eroded horizon sit under a muted dusty-peach sky. Operational survey photograph, candid and restrained, no landing drama, no people, no flags, no text, no logo overlays.
rh01.reference_style: Photograph of a tangible full-size robotic field vehicle, not a miniature. Restrained saturation, natural tonal transitions, fine material texture, matte painted panels, subdued brushed-metal reflections, small dark sensor lenses, plausible scale, and securely mounted equipment. No glossy toy finish, theatrical bloom, captions, graphic overlays, or artificial hero lighting.
rh01.scene_style: Barren Martian terrain: fine rusty ochre dust, dark basalt fragments, dry gravel, weathered layered outcrops, and a distant eroded horizon under a muted dusty-peach sky. No plants, cities, open water, people, or real agency equipment. Believable terrain scale and distant atmospheric haze.
canonical_variants: Keep the arm fully folded into its front travel cradle and make all six wheel positions mechanically plausible.
Use a slightly lower camera and a compact, low-slung rover stance; keep the folded arm entirely below mast height.
Use a higher front-left engineering view with enough clearance to read the mesh wheels, suspension links, instrument deck, and folded arm.
Use a level front-left reference view with the rover compact in frame; keep the mast short and the folded arm visibly stowed against the front body.
scene_variants: Use quiet early-morning side light and faint shallow tracks curving away behind the rover.
Use muted overcast dusty light and a low dark basalt outcrop beyond the rover.
Use late-afternoon cross light and a few wind-rippled patches of fine dust around the wheels.
Use calm diffuse peach-sky light and a distant layered ridge, with no dramatic weather.
